title: 2008年考研英语一 Part B · 七选五

sentences: Directions;
In the following text, some segments have been removed.
For Questions 41—45, choose the most suitable one from the list A-G to fit into each of the numbered blanks.
There are two extra choices, which do not fit in any of the blanks.
Mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET 1.
(10 points)
translations: 说明；
在下面的文本中，一些段落已被移除。
对于问题41—45，从列表A-G中选择最合适的一个填入每个编号的空白处。
有两个额外的选项，它们不适合任何空白处。
在答题卡1上标记你的答案。

sentences: The time for sharpening pencils, arranging your desk, and doing almost anything else instead of writing has ended.
The first draft will appear on the page only if you stop avoiding the inevitable and sit, stand up, or lie down to write.
translations: 削铅笔、整理书桌以及做几乎任何其他事情而不是写作的时间已经结束了。
只有当你停止逃避不可避免的事情，坐下来、站起来或躺下来写作时，初稿才会出现在纸上。

sentences: Be flexible.
Your outline should smoothly conduct you from one point to the next, but do not permit it to railroad you.
If a relevant and important idea occurs to you now, work it into the draft.
(42) Grammar, punctuation, and spelling can wait until you revise.
Concentrate on what you are saying.
Good writing most often occurs when you are in hot pursuit of an idea rather than in a nervous search for errors.
translations: 要灵活。
你的提纲应该顺利地引导你从一个点过渡到下一个点，但不要让它强迫你。
如果现在有一个相关且重要的想法出现在你脑海中，把它写进草稿中。
(42) 语法、标点和拼写可以等到你修改时再处理。
专注于你正在说的内容。
好的写作通常发生在你热烈追求一个想法时，而不是在紧张地寻找错误时。

sentences: (43) Your pages will be easier to keep track of that way, and, if you have to clip a paragraph to place it elsewhere, you will not lose any writing on the other side.
translations: (43) 这样你的页面会更容易跟踪，而且如果你必须剪下一段放在其他地方，你不会丢失另一面的任何文字。

sentences: If you are working on a word processor, you can take advantage of its capacity to make additions and deletions as well as move entire paragraphs by making just a few simple keyboard commands.
Some software programs can also check spelling and certain grammatical elements in your writing.
(44) These printouts are also easier to read than the screen when you work on revisions.
translations: 如果你在文字处理器上工作，你可以利用其添加和删除以及移动整个段落的能力，只需几个简单的键盘命令。
一些软件程序还可以检查你写作中的拼写和某些语法元素。
(44) 当你进行修改时，这些打印输出也比屏幕更容易阅读。

sentences: Once you have a first draft on paper, you can delete material that is unrelated to your thesis and add material necessary to illustrate your points and make your paper convincing.
The student who wrote “The A & P as a State of Mind” wisely dropped a paragraph that questioned whether Sammy displays chauvinistic attitudes toward women.
translations: 一旦你在纸上有了初稿，你可以删除与你的论点无关的材料，并添加必要的材料来阐明你的观点并使你的论文有说服力。
写“The A & P as a State of Mind”的学生明智地删掉了一段质疑Sammy是否对女性表现出沙文主义态度的段落。

sentences: Remember that your initial draft is only that.
You should go through the paper many times—and then again—working to substantiate and clarify your ideas.
You may even end up with several entire versions of the paper.
Rewrite.
The sentences within each paragraph should be related to a single topic.
Transitions should connect one paragraph to the next so that there are no abrupt or confusing shifts.
Awkward or wordy phrasing or unclear sentences and paragraphs should be mercilessly poked and prodded into shape.
translations: 记住，你的初稿只是初稿。
你应该多次通读论文——然后再一次——努力充实和澄清你的想法。
你甚至可能最终得到几个完整的论文版本。
重写。
每个段落内的句子应该与一个主题相关。
过渡应该连接一个段落与下一个段落，这样就不会有突然或令人困惑的转变。
笨拙或冗长的措辞或不清晰的句子和段落应该被无情地推敲和塑造。

sentences: [A] To make revising easier, leave wide margins and extra space between lines so that you can easily add words, sentences, and corrections.
Write on only one side of the paper.
translations: [A] 为了使修改更容易，留出宽边距和行间额外空间，这样你可以轻松添加单词、句子和更正。
只在纸的一面上写。

sentences: [B] After you have clearly and adequately developed the body of your paper, pay particular attention to the introductory and concluding paragraphs.
It’s probably best to write the introduction last, after you know precisely what you are introducing.
Concluding paragraphs demand equal attention because they leave the reader with a final impression.
translations: [B] 在你清晰充分地发展了论文的主体之后，特别注意引言和结论段落。
最好最后写引言，在你确切知道你要介绍什么之后。
结论段落需要同样的关注，因为它们给读者留下最终印象。

sentences: [C] It’s worth remembering, however, that though a clean copy fresh off a printer may look terrific, it will read only as well as the thinking and writing that have gone into it.
Many writers prudently store their data on disks and print their pages each time they finish a draft to avoid losing any material because of power failures or other problems.
translations: [C] 然而，值得记住的是，尽管刚从打印机出来的干净副本可能看起来很棒，但它的阅读效果只取决于投入其中的思考和写作。
许多作家谨慎地将数据存储在磁盘上，并在每次完成草稿时打印页面，以避免因停电或其他问题丢失任何材料。

sentences: [D] It makes no difference how you write, just so you do.
Now that you have developed a topic into a tentative thesis, you can assemble your notes and begin to flesh out whatever outline you have made.
translations: [D] 你怎么写并不重要，只要你在写就行。
既然你已经将一个主题发展成一个初步的论点，你可以整理你的笔记，并开始充实你所做的任何提纲。

sentences: [E] Although this is an interesting issue, it has nothing to do with the thesis, which explains how the setting influences Sammy’s decision to quit his job.
Instead of including that paragraph, she added one that described Lengel’s crabbed response to the girls so that she could lead up to the A & P “policy” he enforces.
translations: [E] 尽管这是一个有趣的问题，但它与论点无关，论点解释了环境如何影响Sammy决定辞职。
她没有包括那一段，而是添加了一段描述Lengel对女孩们暴躁反应的段落，以便她可以引出他所执行的A & P“政策”。

sentences: [F] In the final paragraph about the significance of the setting in “A & P,” the student brings together the reasons Sammy quit his job by referring to his refusal to accept Lengel’s store policies.
translations: [F] 在关于“A & P”中环境重要性的最后一段中，学生通过提到Sammy拒绝接受Lengel的商店政策，将Sammy辞职的原因结合在一起。

sentences: [G] By using the first draft as a means of thinking about what you want to say, you will very likely discover more than your notes originally suggested.
Plenty of good writers don’t use outlines at all but discover ordering principles as they write.
Do not attempt to compose a perfectly correct draft the first time around.
translations: [G] 通过将初稿作为思考你想说什么的手段，你很可能会发现比你的笔记最初建议的更多。
许多优秀作家根本不使用提纲，而是在写作时发现排序原则。
不要试图第一次就写出完全正确的草稿。
